title: Ack processing stall in regional controller led to transient region loss and aggressive variant ramp; routing heal & variant-safety remediation
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary:
On 2026-01-16 22:14 UTC a Cascade-of-Fallbacks incident began when the regional controller's ACK processing queue stalled for ~7 minutes. Nodes in the us-west region were briefly marked unhealthy by the routing control plane. The routing layer responded by draining traffic and failing over to cheaper variants in other regions, which triggered a surge of fallback requests and downstream capacity pressure that amplified latency and error rates for several customers.

Impact:
- Several production customers experienced elevated latency and 5xxs for ~10–25 minutes depending on routing path.
- Autoscale policies in Dedicated pools over-reacted to the surge causing thrash.
- Token-level cost spiked due to repeated reruns on fallback variants and retries.

Root cause (summary):
- The regional controller's ACK consumer experienced a GC/clog event under a large heartbeat reconciliation wave. ACK dequeue paused, leaving decommission/health messages un-ACKed and inflight tombstones not applied.
- The control plane's health aggregator treated the absence of ACKs as explicit negative signals and transitioned nodes to a draining state with low TTLs.
- Smart routing's compatibility matching logic (variant map) was overly eager: when it saw drained nodes, it immediately routed to lower-tier model variants without soft-decline windows, creating a positive feedback loop.
- Lack of an anti-amplification guard on fallbacks (rate-limiting of fallback routing + cross-region surge damping) allowed the fallback surge to cascade into capacity pressure in other regions.

Mitigations applied during incident:
- Rolled back the aggressive draining threshold to a conservative value (control-plane config rollback) — Deploy ID: github.com/redwood/ctrl-plane/PR-7421
- Introduced an emergency routing gate to hold new cross-region fallback traffic for 3 minutes while we stabilized: temp policy applied at 2026-01-16 22:23 UTC
- Increased ACK consumer concurrency and restarted regional-controller pods in a staggered fashion to avoid synchronized reconcilers
- Disabled immediate variant downgrade (patched in-flight compatibility mapping)

Post-incident findings and decisions:
- Short-term (hotfixes):
  - Add backpressure on ACK ingestion: cap requeue frequency and add exponential jitter to reconciliation loops (PR: github.com/redwood/ctrl-plane/pull/7430).
  - Introduce a soft-decline window (30s default) before routing to lower-tier variants. Routing will mark variants as "soft-decline" and only route a bounded percentage during the window.
  - Add a per-customer fallback rate limit and cross-region surge throttle to the smart router.
- Long-term (next quarter):
  - Rework tombstone TTL propagation: ensure decommission tombstones cannot be applied without multiple corroborating signals from heartbeats and capacity API (design doc: confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUN/Tombstone+Hardening).
  - Implement a fallback amplification metric + alerting in Console: ratio of fallback requests to origin requests over rolling 1m and 10m windows.
  - Explore an out-of-band compatibility cache to prevent repeated variant remapping during transient control-plane instability.

Action items and owners:
- ACK backpressure & jitter: owner Alex Romero, estimate 3 pts, due 2026-02-05 (ENG-46120 as follow-up).
- Soft-decline window in router: owner Priya Singh (routing team), estimate 5 pts, due 2026-02-12 (ENG-46121).
- Fallback rate limiter + cross-region throttle: owner Samir Patel (capacity team), estimate 5 pts, due 2026-02-15 (ENG-46122).
- Console metrics & alerting: owner Lina Park (observability), estimate 3 pts, due 2026-02-28.

Rollout plan:
- Hotfixes will ship to runtime-2.3 as small, gated PRs with canary traffic at 1% per region. The soft-decline window will be feature-flagged and enabled behind an org-level flag for 2 weeks before full rollout.

Links / artifacts:
- Incident timeline & raw traces: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/incident/2026-01-16-ack-stall
- Control plane PR: https://github.com/redwood/ctrl-plane/pull/7430
- Router soft-decline spike detector PR: https://github.com/redwood/router/pull/1889
- Design doc (tombstone hardening): https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=87642
- Post-incident cost dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/d/costs/fallback-spike-01-16

decision_log: Keep draining thresholds conservative by default (decision 2026-01-17) — reduces false-positive drains during transient control-plane noise.
Introduce soft-decline windows before variant downgrades (decision 2026-01-18) — reduces amplification of fallbacks.
Add fallback amplification alerting to Console (decision 2026-01-22) — monitoring to detect similar incidents earlier.
